speaker.name: Kelbin Cobb
style_phrases: ends a point with a flat 'That's the lot.'
colour_lines: The great orrery is wound each dawn by the youngest scribe, as a rite of passage.
Strangers are welcome around the Orrery Library, so long as they say good evening.
own_lines: I was left at a shrine gate as an infant and raised by its keepers.
I spent four years pouring bronze for bells. I can still hear a flat note across a street.
I watched two old friends part over a trivial thing after forty years. I decided never to let a small quarrel grow.
My word is the one coin I carry that cannot be forged. I spend it carefully.
I promised someone dear that I would see a particular thing done. I mean to keep my word.
I want to go home. I cannot until this is done.
I want to go home. I cannot until this is finished.

I am a guard at the Orrery Library, and I stand in your way.
By order of the watch, the steady lantern stays here.
Corwin and I were friends once, before things went wrong.

exchanges.hero_words: Kelbin Cobb, who are you, and why do you block the road?
exchanges.reply: Right. I was left at a shrine gate as an infant and raised by its keepers. I poured bronze for bells for four years; why I block the road, I don't know. That's the lot.

exchanges.hero_words: Kelbin Cobb, What do you want from us?
exchanges.reply: Right. I want to go home, and I gave my word to someone dear that I’d see a thing done. My word’s the one coin I carry that can’t be forged. That’s the lot.

exchanges.hero_words: Kelbin Cobb, What will you do if we refuse?
exchanges.reply: Right. Then I still cannot go home; I cannot leave this unfinished. That's the lot.

exchanges.hero_words: Kelbin Cobb, Is there any way to end this without a fight?
exchanges.reply: Right. Corwin and I were friends once, before things went wrong. I watched two old friends part over a small quarrel after forty years; I won't let ours grow. Can we settle this with words?
